extracted.intended_audience: general readers, students, researchers, and policymakers interested in the World Bank Group and international development
extracted.subtask_description: Summarize the World Bank Group's operational policies, safeguards, governance rules, and funding/award criteria as described in the Wikipedia article. Covers lending instruments, safeguards, governance (voting and presidency), and select programmatic policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental and social safeguards (overall)
rubrics_metrics.description: To ensure that World Bank‑financed operations do not compromise these goals but instead add to their realisation, the following environmental, social, and legal safeguards were defined: Environmental Assessment, Indigenous Peoples, Involuntary Resettlement, Physical Cultural Resources, Forests, Natural Habitats, Pest Management, Safety of Dams, Projects in Disputed Areas, Projects on International Waterways, and Performance Standards for Private Sector Activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A review of these safeguards was initiated in 2012; the World Bank developed a new Environmental and Social Framework, implemented since 1 October 2018, to replace/update previous safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental Assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Listed as one of the World Bank's environmental, social, and legal safeguards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the safeguards package intended to ensure financed operations avoid or mitigate environmental harms; review and replacement by the 2018 Environmental and Social Framework noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indigenous Peoples safeguard / policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Indigenous Peoples is named among the Bank's safeguards; the Extractive Industries Review highlighted indigenous peoples' rights, noting critics wanted 'consent' for projects to proceed but the Bank's Management Response used 'consultation'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The EIR process led the World Bank to issue a revised Policy on Indigenous Peoples. The page records the policy tension between 'consent' and 'consultation' and that the Management Response weakened the consent recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Involuntary Resettlement
rubrics_metrics.description: Named as one of the Bank's safeguards to manage projects that physically displace people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the safeguards package; intended to protect affected populations from harm due to displacement; incorporated into the broader Environmental and Social Framework implemented in 2018.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical Cultural Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Listed among the Bank's safeguards to protect cultural heritage affected by projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the discrete safeguard topics the Bank requires consideration of in financed operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forests
rubrics_metrics.description: Named as a specific safeguard area to address impacts of Bank‑financed projects on forest resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the Bank's environmental and social safeguard suite and reviewed as part of the 2012–2018 safeguards reform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural Habitats
rubrics_metrics.description: Included as a safeguard area to avoid or mitigate project impacts on ecological habitats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrated into safeguard reviews and the 2018 Environmental and Social Framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pest Management
rubrics_metrics.description: Listed as one of the Bank's safeguards to address risks from pest management activities financed by projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to ensure pest control interventions do not create undue environmental or health harms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety of Dams
rubrics_metrics.description: Included in the Bank's safeguards to ensure dam projects meet safety standards and avoid downstream harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of project due diligence and safeguard compliance procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projects in Disputed Areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Named as a safeguard topic to address the special risks and sensitivities of projects located in disputed territories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires particular legal and social assessment before proceeding with financing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projects on International Waterways
rubrics_metrics.description: Included as a safeguard to manage transboundary water issues arising from financed projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Triggered when projects may affect water resources shared with other states; entails additional procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance Standards for Private Sector Activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Performance Standards for Private Sector Activities are listed among safeguards, applying particularly to the Bank's private‑sector arm (IFC) and relevant private‑sector financing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to set expectations for private‑sector projects on environmental/social performance; subject to the 2018 framework and ongoing institutional practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lending conditionality / policy‑linked loans
rubrics_metrics.description: Loans or grants for specific projects are often linked to wider policy changes in the sector or the country's economy as a whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example given: a loan to improve coastal environmental management may be linked to development of new environmental institutions at national and local levels and implementation of new regulations to limit pollution. Implies Bank financing may be conditional on policy reforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negative pledge clause
rubrics_metrics.description: The World Bank's negative pledge clause prohibits its debtor countries from using public assets to repay other creditors before they repay the World Bank.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contractual clause in Bank lending agreements to protect its creditor position; cited in Bank operational description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Country Assistance Strategy (CAS) / country programming
rubrics_metrics.description: As a guideline to the World Bank's operations in any particular country, a Country Assistance Strategy is produced in cooperation with the local government and any interested stakeholders and may rely on analytical work performed by the bank or other parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CAS/Country Assistance Strategy is the Bank's country‑level planning tool; it coordinates Bank operations with government priorities and stakeholder input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poverty reduction strategies and IDA assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: For the poorest developing countries, the Bank's assistance plans are based on poverty reduction strategies; by combining an analysis of local groups with an analysis of the country's financial and economic situation the World Bank develops a plan pertaining to the country in question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The government then identifies priorities and targets for poverty reduction and the Bank instigates aid accordingly. IDA distributes concessional finance (interest‑free loans or grants) to the poorest countries; IDA is core funding for those countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Development Marketplace Awards selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The Development Marketplace Awards is a grant program that surfaces and funds development projects with potential for development impact that are scalable or replicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grant beneficiaries are social enterprises with projects that aim to deliver social and public services to groups with the lowest incomes — scalability/replicability and development impact are explicit selection criteria (per the article).

rubrics_metrics.name: Voting power and governance rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Voting powers at the World Bank are allocated based on subscriptions to capital (one vote per share) with additional votes related to financial contributions; voting power is roughly proportional to shareholding. Changes to the Bank's Charter require an 85% supermajority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voice Reform – Phase 2 revised votes to increase developing countries' representation; voting adjustments were described as aiming for more rule‑based objective indicators and transparency. The U.S.'s large share has formal blocking capacity for charter changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: President selection and term
rubrics_metrics.description: Traditionally, the Bank president has been a U.S. citizen nominated by the president of the United States; the nominee is subject to confirmation by the Bank's executive directors and serves a five‑year, renewable term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article notes the tradition and practical influence this yields, and that the president chairs board meetings and directs overall management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open data / Open Knowledge Repository standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The World Bank has made data and models available to the public and recent publications are available as open access under a Creative Commons Attribution License; the Bank hosts the Open Knowledge Repository as an official open access repository.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This openness is intended to encourage reuse; the Bank received the SPARC Innovator 2012 award for this approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extractive Industries Review recommendations (fossil fuels) and indigenous consent vs consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Extractive Industries Review (EIR) concluded fossil fuel and mining projects do not alleviate poverty and recommended phasing out World Bank involvement in these sectors and that indigenous peoples and affected communities should provide 'consent' for projects to proceed; the Bank's Management Response did not accept many conclusions and replaced 'consent' with 'consultation'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EIR influenced Bank policy changes and led to a revised Policy on Indigenous Peoples, but the Management Response weakened some recommendations; the EIR is cited as a major independent review shaping policy debate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pandemic Emergency Financing Facility (PEF) design constraint
rubrics_metrics.description: The PEF's terms prevent any money from being released from the fund until 12 weeks after the outbreak was initially detected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This design feature was criticized for causing a slow response in the COVID‑19 pandemic even though other eligibility requirements were met; cited as an operational design criterion with consequences for timeliness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Climate finance / fossil fuel financing policy (announced position vs practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: In December 2017 the World Bank announced it would no longer finance fossil fuel development, but reporting and civil society groups have accused the Bank of continuing to finance fossil fuel infrastructure and not having meaningfully shifted away.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This highlights a policy standard (no fossil fuel financing) and the critique/implementation gap; calls from activists and some governments for ending fossil fuel funding are noted, as is Bank participation in climate finance instruments (e.g., hosting Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage).

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional roles / instrument eligibility (IBRD, IDA, IFC, MIGA, ICSID)
rubrics_metrics.description: The World Bank Group comprises five institutions with distinct instruments and eligibility: IBRD provides debt financing based on sovereign guarantees; IDA provides concessional financing (interest‑free loans or grants), usually with sovereign guarantees; IFC provides various forms of financing without sovereign guarantees, primarily to the private sector; MIGA provides insurance (political risk insurance) primarily to the private sector; ICSID works with governments to reduce investment risk through dispute settlement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These role definitions function as operational criteria for which instrument is used for what borrower or activity (sovereign vs private, concessional vs commercial, insurance vs dispute settlement).
